title: Supervisory Stress Test Documentation Market Risk Models

source.name: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System

summary: The Federal Reserve published comprehensive technical documentation detailing the market risk models to be used in the 2026 Supervisory Stress Test, covering Securities, Fair Value Option, Yield Curve, Private Equity, Trading P&L, Trading Issuer Default Loss, CVA, and Largest Counterparty Default models. This document provides model specifications, calibration rationale, alternative approaches considered, and data adjustments for each component.
key_points: Covers 8 model categories: Securities Model, Fair Value Option Model, Yield Curve Model, Private Equity Model, Trading P&L Model, Trading Issuer Default Loss Model, CVA Model, and LCPD Model
Updated January 2026, originally published October 2025, for use in the 2026 Supervisory Stress Test
Each model section includes statement of purpose, model overview, specification details, calibration rationale, alternative approaches, data adjustments, and assumptions/limitations
Yield Curve Model covers Treasury, SOFR, and Corporate rate modeling components
CVA Model includes both Standard and Non-Standard approaches for credit valuation adjustment calculations
Trading Issuer Default Loss Model includes technical specification by portfolio segment and calibration details
why_it_matters: This documentation is critical for large banks and trading desks to understand how the Federal Reserve will model market risk under stress scenarios. Banks subject to the supervisory stress test must align their internal models and risk calculations with Fed methodology to pass the test. The document reveals how the Fed will stress credit spreads, yields, counterparty defaults, and trading losses.
market_structure_context: Defines the regulatory framework and methodology for how the Fed models market risk in bank stress tests, including yield curves (Treasury, SOFR, corporate), credit risk (CVA, default losses), and counterparty exposure (LCPD).
